answer: An AI-agent market requires every active seller identity to lock a separate bond in escrow; the same funds cannot back two accounts. If a seller takes payment but fails to deliver a cryptographically verifiable result by its deadline, the bond is slashed. Each identity is an island of collateral, so a ripple of new aliases gives no free capacity. An attacker’s ivory tower of fake sellers requires capital proportional to its size and loses that capital on provable defaults.
